name: PT Lippo Karawaci Tbk

frontmatter.title: Lippo Karawaci: an asset case priced at our bear case
frontmatter.summary: LPKR trades at a tenth of book and a discount to our RNAV close to the level our bear case implies. The operating evidence is intact - presales running at the full-year target, a recurring arm that services a third of interest - but the call is an asset call, not an earnings one, and the earned discount is the risk.
thesis: The price already embeds the bear case: at today's discount the shares sit where our no-narrowing scenario puts them, so the downside in the asset value is largely paid for.

The operating base is intact on the nine-month actuals: marketing sales are running at the full-year target, EBITDA holds the nine-month run-rate, and the lifestyle arm earns a third of the group's interest bill.
The target rests on RNAV; on the peer P/E the shares are already at fair value, so we do not claim an earnings re-rating.
The balance sheet has been transformed but not fixed: debt has halved since the Siloam sell-down, yet about half of it is now current and must be refinanced.
Governance is the kill risk and the discount is its price; we assume only partial mean-reversion, to the peer median P/B of just under a third of book, never to NAV.

catalysts.event: Fourth-quarter marketing-sales release: trigger is a full-year print below the 2026 target, which would break the operating base the base case rests on
FY2026 audited results: trigger is the related-party note and the terms on which the current debt is refinanced
Any board resolution to monetise land, a mall or the Siloam stake; the resolution itself, not the rumour, is the trigger

blocks.text: We stay at **BUY** with a twelve-month target of **Rp103**, a total return of **129.5%** from Rp45. The target is higher than the previous version because the discount it was anchored on did not match the evidence: the peer median P/B is just under a third of book, not the fifth the note claimed, and the target now sits at that median rather than below LPKR's own five-year band [S0]. The value before the twelve-month cost-of-equity roll is Rp105, and the difference is the required return the rating bands are calibrated on; a reader who thinks an asset value should not accrete at the cost of equity should use the lower figure. The operating view is unchanged: the third quarter's profit was not operating profit, and the bear case must allow the discount to persist [S0][S14].

What changed. The earnings base is now built from the nine-month actuals rather than calibrated to a chosen output: other non-operating income is IDR500.0bn, the run-rate the statements show once the third quarter's one-off is removed, instead of a plug [S0]. The blend is 75% on RNAV and 25% on P/E applied to FY2025 underlying earnings, using the median of the six covered township developers, which is 4.8 times; the P/B leg is gone because it applied a pre-deconsolidation multiple to a book that doubled with the Siloam deal [S0]. The land bank is now carried at book net of the non-debt current liabilities that fund it, rather than gross [S0]. The RNAV discount is re-anchored on the evidence: the engine's peer median P/B is just under a third of book and LPKR's own four-year average is a little above that, so the target sits just under a third of book rather than under a fifth as in the previous version, which was a bearish judgment presented as a peer median [S0]. And the bear holds the discount at today's level with half the probability, because that is the scenario the price is already discounting.

The variant view. The market is not paying for the land bank, the malls or the Siloam stake: the carrying value of the investments line alone exceeds the market capitalisation [S0][S9]. We do not argue that gap closes. We argue that the shares trade at the level our no-narrowing scenario produces, so a holder is paid to wait for partial mean-reversion, and the things that would force a re-rating - a refinancing at a sane cost, a land or mall sale at book, a distribution of the Siloam stake - are identifiable and dated [S9][S14].

What moves the value. First, the discount: it is three quarters of the target and the largest sensitivity in the grid. Second, the RNAV itself: the malls and hotels at a capitalisation rate and the land at cost are the two components, and a land sale at our carrying value would validate the second [S13]. Third, the refinancing: 5.6 times net debt to EBITDA with about half the debt - a little under half of the nearly nine trillion rupiah total - classified current is the constraint on the whole asset case [S0].

Lippo Karawaci is one of the oldest township developers in Indonesia and has been through a full cycle of expansion, leverage, restructuring and asset sales. Its history is well known to local investors, and the market's scepticism about related-party dealing and dilution is not new. What has changed is the shape of the company: it is smaller, less levered, and its listed healthcare asset is now an investment rather than a consolidated division.

LPKR operates two reported segments. Real estate develops and sells landed housing, commercial units and land plots across integrated townships, and generated IDR7,670.0bn of revenue in FY2025, a 52.0% increase year on year [S13]. Lifestyle runs the shopping malls and the Aryaduta hotel business and generated IDR1,370.0bn in the same year, with gross profit of IDR1,030.0bn and EBITDA of IDR448.0bn [S13]. The company describes itself as an integrated real estate platform with a presence across the archipelago and a developable land bank of 1,380 ha hectares, developed through the flagship Lippo Village in Tangerang and through two listed subsidiaries, Lippo Cikarang and Gowa Makassar Tourism [S15].

The portfolio also includes Lippo Cikarang, Tanjung Bunga, Royal Serpong Village and San Diego Hills Memorial Park, according to the company's description of its projects [S5]. The healthcare arm is no longer consolidated: after selling an IDR6,900.0bn slice of Siloam in September 2024, LPKR retained a 29.1% stake and carries it as an investment [S9]. That transaction explains most of the difference between the FY2024 reported result and today's earnings base, and it is why the data pack's pre-2025 history is not comparable with the business as it stands [S0][S9].

Strategically, management has narrowed to real estate and lifestyle, with capital discipline, cost control and debt reduction as stated priorities [S13]. The mix is deliberately weighted to affordable and mid-market landed housing: in the first nine months of 2026 landed homes were the bulk of marketing sales, and the company launched Park Serpong phases seven and eight and Hunian Warisan Bangsa Serang, at affordable price points aimed at first-time buyers [S11][S14]. In the lifestyle arm, hotel occupancy was 54.0% at an average room rate of about 635 IDR thousand rupiah, and mall footfall averaged 11.2 million visits/month million visitors a month [S11].

The controlling shareholder is the Riady family's Lippo group, which holds the large majority of the shares and is represented on the board. The free float is 38.0% on the exchange registry, which is the figure we use; the data pack's insider share of 67.7% is measured on a different basis and counts group cross-holdings, so the two are not additive and a sum above a hundred per cent is a definitional artefact rather than a data error [S0]. LPKR is a holding structure in practice: the value of the listed subsidiaries and the Siloam stake sits alongside the directly owned townships, which is why we value it on a sum-of-assets basis rather than on earnings alone [S15][S9]. The revenue mix in the forecast follows the segment disclosure rather than the consolidated total: real estate is the swing factor and lifestyle is the annuity. Within real estate, the company distinguishes residential sales in the holding company, commercial unit sales, high-rise inventory and land plots, which is a more granular mix than the segment line shows and one we monitor because commercial and land sales carry different margins from landed housing [S4][S11].

Indonesian landed housing is a mortgage-driven business, and the transmission channel runs from the policy rate through bank lending rates to affordability and launch take-up. The macro deck has the BI rate at 5.8% through the forecast horizon, so we are not underwriting a rate-cut cycle [S0]. The rupiah path in the same deck is Rp18,350/USD against a spot of about eighteen thousand rupiah per dollar, and we use that path rather than a flat exchange rate wherever dollar exposure matters, because it does not help this name: the company has not disclosed the currency split of its debt, so the deck's weaker rupiah is a risk to interest cost, not a tailwind [S0]. That matters: the base case cannot lean on cheaper mortgages, and volume has to come from the affordable segment's own demand and from the launch programme [S11].

The competitive set is the listed township developers, and LPKR is a challenger rather than the leader by scale. Its differentiation is land: a large, contiguous, largely paid-for land bank in established townships gives it a cost advantage on affordable products that developers buying land today cannot match [S15]. The weakness is execution and balance-sheet history, not product. The townships are integrated - housing, retail, hospitality and historically healthcare - which supports pricing and recurring income, but also means capital is tied up in infrastructure that only pays back through years of sales [S5].

Demand in the affordable segment has been resilient through a weak consumer environment: first-time buyers and end-users dominate sales, with 72.0% of first-half sales financed through mortgages and the proportion rising in the third quarter [S11][S14]. That is a healthier mix than investor-driven high-rise presales, because end-user demand is stickier and cancellations are lower, but it is more sensitive to monthly instalments and therefore to rates [S4].

On the five-forces view [S5], rivalry among developers is high and product is substitutable; buyer power is moderate because mortgage availability, not price negotiation, is the binding constraint; supplier power sits with contractors and materials, where cost inflation is the main margin risk; the threat of new entrants is high at project level but low at township level, because assembling a comparable land position in Tangerang is no longer possible at LPKR's cost; and substitutes are second-hand homes and rental. The moat is the land bank and the township infrastructure, not the brand. Demand is also geographically concentrated: Tangerang and the greater Jakarta fringe carry the bulk of the landed business, with Cikarang and Makassar as the second and third legs through the listed subsidiaries [S15][S5]. That concentration is a strength while those catchments grow and a vulnerability if local infrastructure or flooding issues appear.

Regulation matters in two directions. Incentives for affordable housing support the segment LPKR sells into, while any tightening of mortgage rules or of the incentive regime would hit take-up directly. We treat policy as a scenario driver rather than a base-case assumption, because the current support has been extended repeatedly and its renewal is not something we can source with confidence [S4].

On the desk stance: the sector view is AVOID on rate-sensitive Indonesian property, and this is a single-name exception, not a sector call. The value here does not depend on a property upcycle: the shares already trade at our no-narrowing scenario, the recurring arm covers a third of the interest bill, and the asset value is carried at book rather than at an appraisal [S0]. We would not own the sector for rate cuts; we own this name for the gap between a book-based asset value and a price that assumes no narrowing of a governance discount.

FY2025 revenue was IDR9,030.0bn with EBITDA of IDR1,370.0bn as the company reports it, and underlying net profit after tax of IDR630.0bn, in a year when consumer demand weakened [S13]. Real estate carried the year at IDR7,670.0bn, up sharply on handovers of residential and commercial units, while lifestyle delivered IDR1,370.0bn of revenue and IDR448.0bn of EBITDA [S13].

Nine-month 2026 revenue of IDR5,370.0bn is lower year on year because the handover calendar is lighter, while reported EBITDA of IDR1,110.0bn and net profit after tax of IDR1,240.0bn are higher [S14]. Those two statements are consistent only once the third quarter is opened up, and this revision does that. On the pack's quarterly statements, third-quarter pre-tax profit exceeded operating profit by more than the whole of FY2025's IDR593.8bn of non-operating income, the cash balance fell, total assets fell, and the effective tax charge on that pre-tax profit was a small fraction of the statutory rate [S0]. The item is a non-cash, non-recurring gain: it is not in operating cash flow, it did not raise cash, and it did not raise the asset base. We therefore exclude it from the earnings base, add nothing to RNAV for it, and deduct nothing either - if it proves to be a disposal, the sold asset's carrying amount has already left the balance sheet we value, so there is no double count [S0].

The earnings bridge from the nine-month actual to our forecast is explicit. Nine-month operating profit, interest, interest income and the residual non-operating line are taken from the statements, and the third-quarter one-off is removed. The fourth quarter is not a plug on the prior year: development revenue is FY2026 marketing sales of about IDR5,490.0bn annualised at the nine-month run-rate, recognised in full in the year of sale by the 1.0 recognition ratio, so the implied fourth quarter is below FY2025's fourth quarter because the nine-month revenue base is itself below last year [S0][S14][S13]. On that build FY2026 revenue of IDR7,422.7bn is below FY2025 because the nine-month actual is below the prior year, and FY2026 parent net profit of IDR514.5bn is below the FY2025 underlying figure of IDR630.0bn for the same reason. Presales and revenue are not the same series: revenue recognises handovers, and the nine-month revenue decline in the actual statements is what governs the year, not the presales growth [S14].

The comparability problem in the data pack is material and we have restated it. FY2024 consolidated Siloam for most of the year, so the pack's revenue for that year includes a healthcare business LPKR no longer owns, and reported net profit is dominated by the gain on deconsolidation [S0][S9]. We restate the FY2025 revenue and underlying net profit lines to the company's own reported figures and let segment facts drive the revenue build, so the forecast starts from the business as it is now rather than from a scope that no longer exists [S13].

Definition matters on EBITDA and this revision separates the two measures rather than blending them. The company's reported EBITDA is higher than the pack's operating measure at every period we can check - IDR1,370.0bn against the pack-consistent figure for FY2025, and IDR1,110.0bn in the nine months against the operating measure implied by the quarterly statements - because the company adds back items the pack keeps in operating cost [S13][S14][S0]. Our forecast is built on the pack-consistent measure, so the history and the forecast sit on one definition; against the company's own measure, FY2026 EBITDA of IDR1,307.6bn is slightly below FY2025's reported figure. The step visible in the table is the nine-month actual level, not an assumption: gross margin on the pack's numbers rose from about a third of revenue in FY2025 to over two fifths in the nine months, driven by commercial and land-plot mix and by cost of revenue falling faster than revenue [S0][S14].

Margins need care in the other direction too. Development gross margin is set at the nine-month actual and then faded back towards, but not to, the FY2025 level, because the nine-month figure is lifted by commercial unit and land-plot sales that will not be a permanent share of handovers [S14][S13]. Lifestyle gross margin is held near 78.0% - between the first-half actual and the FY2025 segment margin - and the operating-cost ratio is set at the nine-month actual, below it nowhere, because the cost base is largely fixed and revenue is still below the FY2025 handover peak [S11][S13][S0].

The balance sheet is the part of the story that has changed but not been fixed. Debt fell from over twenty-one trillion rupiah in FY2022 to single digits by FY2025, and cash was IDR1,960.0bn at the year end and IDR1,370.0bn at the third quarter as the company reports it [S0][S13][S4]. On the third-quarter balance, net debt of a little over seven trillion rupiah against last-twelve-month EBITDA of about one and a quarter trillion is close to six times, and our FY2026 estimate of 5.6 times holds net debt flat at the 30 September level rather than assuming a year-end paydown [S0][S14]. That is high in absolute terms and serviced by a recurring EBITDA stream and by a land bank that can be monetised, but the maturity profile is the sharper issue: about half the debt - a little under half of the nearly nine trillion rupiah total - is classified current on the third-quarter balance sheet [S0]. That is a refinancing task, not a liquidity crisis, and it is the single most important thing to watch in the FY2026 accounts.

Cash flow is dominated by inventory and by the run-off of customer advances. The land bank and work in progress sit in working capital, so operating cash flow swings with the handover calendar and with land purchases rather than tracking profit [S0]. We hold inventory growing with revenue in absolute terms, because land does not shrink with sales and the actual record shows no year-end release: operating cash flow was negative by about a third of a trillion rupiah in the nine months to September 2026 and by about two fifths of a trillion in the fourth quarter of FY2025, so the forecast carries no fourth-quarter collection windfall [S0][S14]. On that path FY2026 free cash flow is IDR218.5bn and net debt ends the year at IDR7,280.4bn, essentially the 30 September balance, rather than the cash build of nearly a trillion rupiah the previous version implied; the working-capital build then resumes with revenue growth, which is why forecast free cash flow is negative in the later years and the reverse DCF does not solve [S0].
Earnings quality is the section the red team was right to press, and we now run the full screen rather than describing it [S0].

| Screen | Reading | Classification | |---|---|---| | Accruals ratio, FY2025 | net profit of about six hundred billion less an operating cash outflow of about one and a half trillion, over average total assets of about fifty-two trillion: about four per cent [S0] | below the ten per cent threshold: no accruals flag | | Accruals trend, FY2023-FY2025 | minus three per cent, plus thirty-three per cent, plus four per cent on the same definition [S0] | FY2024 is an artefact, not a finding: the eighteen trillion rupiah deconsolidation gain never passed through cash, and adjusting it out turns the ratio negative. FY2025 is clean at about four per cent | | Cash conversion FY2025 | free cash flow of IDR-1,032.6bn against net profit of IDR572.5bn [S0] | optics class: the gap is a rundown of customer advances and payables, disclosed and explained, not a receivables build | | Nine-month 2026 cash flow | operating cash outflow of about a third of a trillion rupiah and a falling cash balance [S0][S14] | watch: the third-quarter gain did not bring cash | | IDX board and notation | no special monitoring-board or notation flag; the high-shareholding-concentration regime that took effect in November 2026 is an index-transparency measure, not a finding of wrongdoing, and does not list LPKR in our registry data | none found - checked [S16] | | Related-party flows | revenue and purchases are not disclosed in any source we can archive as at 15 November 2026 [S0] | open, recorded as a kill criterion: to be closed with the FY2026 annual report, due March 2027, and a refusal to disclose would itself be a red flag |

On capital allocation, with no dividend the cash goes to debt service, maintenance capex and a modest buyback: the treasury shares bought in earlier years were cancelled at the September 2026 extraordinary meeting [S0][S17]. Retiring debt and buying stock at a deep discount to asset value is the right use of cash here, but the buyback is small against the market capitalisation, so it supports the price at the margin rather than re-rating it.

We value LPKR on RNAV, weighted at three quarters of the target, with a P/E cross-check weighted at a quarter. That is the right method set for a developer whose earnings describe handovers from land bought years ago: the P&L understates the value of the land bank, and a discounted cash flow on a lumpy handover profile is unstable and, in this case, not even available as a bracket for the price. RNAV is the only method that values what the company actually owns, and because we carry the land at book rather than at an appraisal, the result is a book-based asset value that a conservative reader can reproduce from the balance sheet [S0].

The RNAV has three components and one deduction beyond net debt. First, the land bank: property inventory at the last reported balance-sheet date, carried at cost, less the non-debt current liabilities that fund it - the customer advances, payables and accruals left after removing current debt from current liabilities. That deduction is the haircut the house card asks for and it is stated rather than implied: the land is valued at book net of buyer claims, with no appraisal uplift added on top [S0]. Second, the malls and hotels: we capitalise the lifestyle segment's gross profit at 19.0%, equivalent to a high-single-digit yield on segment EBITDA and in line with where Indonesian retail and hotel portfolios transact [S13]. Third, the investments line, largely the 29.1% Siloam stake, is taken at its balance-sheet carrying amount [S9][S0]. Net debt and minorities are deducted. The pack discloses inventory as a single line, so land, work in progress and completed stock cannot be split without the LK note; we value the whole balance at book and say so rather than implying a split we do not have [S0].

The result is RNAV per share of many times the current price and we apply a target discount of 71.0%. The discount is anchored on the evidence rather than on a judgment dressed as one. Because our RNAV is book-based, the comparable is the peer P/B, and the engine's peer table gives a median of just under a third of book - CTRA near a third, BSDE a fifth, SMRA a third, ASRI and APLN under a fifth, PWON over a half - while LPKR's own four-year average is a little above a third, inside a band of a fifth to a little under a half before the 2024 Siloam deconsolidation [S0]. A discount of 71.0% puts the target just under a third of book: the peer median, the bottom of the peer range, and inside LPKR's own band. That is a correction to the previous version, which applied a target under a fifth of book and attributed it to a peer median of about a fifth that the peer table does not show; that was a bearish judgment and should have been labelled as one. The risk that justified it - leverage of close to six times and the governance history - is now carried where it belongs: in the bear case, which holds the shares at today's discount of roughly nine tenths and carries half the probability [S0][S14]. So the target is not NAV convergence. It is the price at which LPKR trades like a normal Indonesian developer again, and the discount stays structural.

The cost of equity build is uncomfortable and we say why: a levered beta above two, driven by the market-value debt-to-equity ratio at a depressed share price, produces a cost of equity of 21.2% [S0]. We do not discount the RNAV at it, because RNAV is an asset value rather than a cash-flow stream. The engine's twelve-month convention rolls the fundamental value forward at that cost of equity, which adds materially to the published target; we disclose the composition rather than hide it, and the undiscounted fundamental value today is Rp105. A reader who thinks an asset value should not accrete at the cost of equity should use Rp105 as the value today and treat the difference as the required return the rating bands are calibrated on.

The P/E cross-check sits well below the RNAV leg, and that is the most important change in this revision. On 4.8 times - the median of the six covered township developers, CTRA, BSDE, SMRA, ASRI, APLN and PWON, rather than the eighty-one-name screen the initiation used - our FY2025 underlying earnings give Rp43, which is below today's share price [S0]. The leg is labelled on FY2025 earnings because that is the last audited underlying number; on our FY2026 estimate it would be lower still, and would move the blend by a couple of rupiah, which does not change the rating. In other words the shares are not cheap on earnings against their peers; they are already at fair value. We keep the cross-check precisely because it says that: the call is an asset call, and if the assets are worth what the balance sheet says, the earnings multiple is irrelevant; if they are not, the earnings multiple is the ceiling. The P/B leg used in the initiation is dropped: it applied a four-observation average earned when book equity was half its current size to a book that doubled with the Siloam deconsolidation, and it was the highest of the three legs because of that arithmetic, not because of anything the market was saying [S0].

What does today's price imply? The reverse DCF does not solve for this name - the engine reports it as unavailable because forecast free cash flow is negative in the working-capital build years - so we do not claim an implied presales path from it. The arithmetic that does hold: the carrying value of the investments line alone, dominated by the Siloam stake, is a multiple of the market capitalisation [S0][S9]. A buyer at today's price is paying very little for the townships and the malls on top of that, though a minority holder cannot force a sale, which is why the asset case is a waiting game rather than an event.

The largest risk is governance and control, and it is not diversifiable. The Riady family controls the company with the large majority of the shares, and the group's history includes related-party transactions, dilution and a debt restructuring that cost minority holders [S0]. A transaction that transfers value from LPKR to another group entity would defeat the asset thesis regardless of RNAV. We found no current pledge or related-party arrangement in the sources we could access, but absence of evidence is not evidence of absence, and the related-party note is the first thing we would close with the annual report [S0].

The second risk is the balance sheet, and the red team sharpened our view of it. Net debt to EBITDA of 5.6 times is high, debt costs close to 8.0%, and about half the debt - a little under half of the nearly nine trillion rupiah total - is current at the third-quarter date [S0][S13]. A refinancing at a higher cost is the plausible mechanism by which the asset value is impaired without any operating deterioration, because interest takes the equity before the land does. We could not source a breakdown of the currency mix of debt, so we cannot rule out dollar exposure; the deck's rupiah path to Rp18,350/USD is the number to apply if the company discloses a dollar share [S0].

The third risk is the one the initiation failed to explain, and we address it directly. The shares have more than halved since the middle of 2025 with no split and no dividend, and the decline was concentrated in three legs: the autumn of 2025, the spring of 2026, and a further leg in September 2026 around the extraordinary meeting that reconstituted the board and cancelled the treasury shares [S0][S17]. The operating news over that period was good - record profits and presales close to target - so the market was not selling earnings. It was selling the equity of a concentrated-ownership developer in a year when the exchange rewrote the index rules for concentrated-ownership names and global index providers froze or cut Indonesian exposure [S16]. That is a plausible, dated explanation, and it is also why we cannot claim the market is wrong: the discount is being set by a regime, not by a modelling error. What we can claim is that the regime is about index mechanics and control, not about the land, and that the price already sits at our no-narrowing scenario.

Fourth, execution: handover timing drives reported revenue, and a slip in construction or permitting moves a year's earnings into the next. Fifth, policy: the affordable-housing incentives and subsidised mortgage quotas supporting LPKR's core segment can be changed, and the segment's mortgage dependence is what makes it rate-sensitive [S11]. Sixth, liquidity: the shares trade a modest daily value, which limits institutional position size and is part of why the discount persists [S0].

The scenario set is now asymmetric on purpose and mirrored on drivers. Bear and bull shock the same three things by mirrored amounts - presales growth by ten percentage points either way, the discount by fifteen points either way, and the capitalisation rate by two points either way - but the bear carries half the probability because the kill risk is governance, not operations [S0]. In the bear the discount barely narrows from today's level, presales stall as mortgage costs stay high, and the refinancing lands at a higher cost; that scenario puts the shares at Rp67, close to today's price. In other words, the current price is the bear. The base case, at a smaller discount than today but still far wider than the sector, gives Rp127; the bull, with a monetisation and a discount back to the top of LPKR's own pre-deconsolidation band, gives Rp190.

The signposts that would change our view. On the downside: a refinancing at a materially higher cost, a covenant breach, or a related-party transaction that moves assets out of LPKR - any of these would defeat the asset case because the value is only accessible if the company is a going concern and the minority shares in it. On the upside: a distribution of the Siloam stake in specie, a sale of township land to a joint-venture partner at or above our carrying value, or a dividend - each would both crystallise asset value and signal that the controlling shareholder is aligned with minorities [S9][S0]. Marketing sales below the prior year for two consecutive quarters is the operating kill criterion.

Ownership is concentrated in the Lippo group, with the free float at 38.0% on the exchange registry and a controlling family represented on the board [S0]. The board was reconstituted at an extraordinary meeting in September 2026, when a commissioner resigned and the remaining commissioners and directors were reappointed to 2028, and the same meeting cancelled the treasury shares held since the buybacks of 2020 to 2023 [S17]. The company has not paid a dividend in the period covered by our data, and capital allocation has gone to debt reduction and a buyback rather than distributions [S0][S13].

On related parties, the group structure is the central governance question: LPKR sits alongside other Lippo vehicles, and the Siloam stake is the kind of asset that can be moved between them [S9]. We found no disclosed pledge of the controlling stake, no auditor qualification and no going-concern note in the sources available to us, but we did not have access to the full annual report, and that is a limitation of this note rather than a clean bill of health. The related-party share of revenue and purchases is not disclosed in the sources we can archive, and we flag it as the largest evidence gap rather than estimating it [S0].

The market-regime overlay matters here and belongs in governance rather than in the industry section. The exchange expanded its high-shareholding-concentration list in November 2026 and excluded those names from the IHSG calculation from the middle of the month, on a methodology that looks at ownership concentration rather than price behaviour; the exchange is explicit that the status is a transparency measure and not a finding of wrongdoing [S16]. LPKR is not on that list in our registry data, but the regime change is why concentrated-ownership names de-rated in 2026 and it is a live risk if the family's stake rises [S16][S0].

ESG exposure is concentrated in land development. On the social side, the townships are long-lived communities and the licence to keep selling depends on how drainage, access and public amenities are managed. On governance, the key test is whether the board's independent members can constrain related-party transactions; the composition changed in 2026 and we will watch the pattern of votes and any new affiliate dealings rather than the stated policy [S0][S5]. The company publishes a sustainability agenda and governance policies on its website [S5]. We do not attempt to quantify an ESG premium or discount, but a serious environmental or community incident in a township would hit presales directly.

The near-term catalyst is the FY2026 results and the 2027 marketing-sales target, together with the refinancing of the current debt, which will show whether the 2026 run-rate is a new level or a good year and at what cost the balance sheet is rolled [S14]. Quarterly marketing-sales updates are the highest-frequency signal and the one we will trade on. On the asset side, any decision to monetise part of the Siloam stake, sell land to a joint-venture partner, or distribute value to shareholders would be the event that narrows the discount [S9].

The KPIs we monitor are marketing sales against target and their landed-versus-high-rise mix, the handover schedule and revenue recognition, lifestyle EBITDA and hotel occupancy, net debt, the current portion of debt and interest cost, and any change in the controlling shareholder's stake or in related-party flows [S14][S11][S13]. A sustained fall in presales, a refinancing above our cost of debt, or a related-party transaction are the three developments that would make us revisit the rating.

bear.narrative: The discount does not narrow at all: presales stall as mortgage costs stay high, the Rp4.2tn of debt classified current is refinanced at a higher cost, and the third-quarter gain is not repeated, so the shares stay at today's roughly 90% discount to RNAV [S0][S14].

bull.narrative: Cheaper mortgages and the affordable-housing credit line lift presales above target, and a land or mall monetisation crystallises asset value, taking the discount back to about 56%, or 0.44x book - the top of LPKR's own pre-deconsolidation P/B band [S14][S16].

sensitivity.title: 12-month value vs presales growth and RNAV discount

assumptions.label: Presales growth
assumptions.basis: FY2025A marketing sales were Rp5.32tn, 85% of target [S13]; nine-month 2026 marketing sales of Rp5.49tn are 91% of the Rp6.03tn 2026 target, so the fourth quarter at the nine-month run-rate takes the year to about Rp6.0tn (+13%) [S14]; growth then normalises to mid-single digits on affordable landed demand with no rate-cut underwriting.

assumptions.label: Share of presales recognised in the same year
assumptions.basis: Held at 1.0 because FY2025 real estate revenue of Rp7.67tn exceeded the FY2025 presales base [S13][S15], so revenue is handover-led and includes land and commercial sales outside marketing sales; recognising presales in-year reproduces the nine-month 2026 development revenue run-rate of Rp4.45tn (group revenue Rp5.37tn less lifestyle Rp922bn) [S14].

assumptions.label: Recurring revenue growth
assumptions.basis: Lifestyle revenue was Rp1.37tn in FY2025 [S13], Rp605bn in the first half of 2026 with 54% hotel occupancy and mall traffic up 1% [S11], and Rp922bn in the nine months with EBITDA of Rp377bn [S14]; the nine-month figure annualises to about Rp1.23tn, so FY2026 growth is set at 3% on the segment's own run-rate and then 6-7% on rent indexation and a hotel recovery.

assumptions.label: Development gross margin
assumptions.basis: Nine-month 2026 group gross profit of Rp2,302bn is 42.5% of revenue; stripping the lifestyle segment's gross profit (about Rp719bn on Rp922bn of revenue) leaves development gross profit of about Rp1,583bn on Rp4,448bn of development revenue, or 36% [S14][S0]. FY2025 was 25.5% (group gross profit less lifestyle's Rp1.03tn over Rp7.67tn) [S13], so the nine-month improvement is a mix effect from commercial and land sales; FY2026 is set at 35% and the margin then fades to the FY2025 level by FY2029 rather than holding the peak.

assumptions.label: Recurring gross margin
assumptions.basis: Lifestyle gross profit was Rp1.03tn on Rp1.37tn of revenue in FY2025 (75%) [S13] and Rp490bn on Rp605bn in the first half of 2026 (81%) [S11]; malls carry high incremental margins on rent indexation, so 78% is used for FY2026 and the level fades to 75% as hotel costs normalise.

assumptions.label: Cap rate for investment property (RNAV)
assumptions.basis: The engine capitalises lifestyle gross profit, not net operating income; 19% on FY2026E gross profit values the malls and hotels at about Rp6.0tn, equal to a 7.4% yield on the segment's FY2025 EBITDA of Rp448bn [S13] - the level at which Indonesian mall and hotel portfolios transact.

assumptions.label: Target discount to RNAV
assumptions.basis: The shares trade near 0.10x book; our RNAV is a book-based asset value (land at cost, malls at a capitalisation rate), so the comparable anchor is the peer P/B and LPKR's own history. The engine's peer table gives a median P/B of 0.2906x across CTRA 0.375, BSDE 0.217, SMRA 0.364, ASRI 0.163, APLN 0.158 and PWON 0.536 [S0], and LPKR's own four-year average P/B is 0.3135x (FY2022A 0.365, FY2023A 0.449, FY2024A 0.242, FY2025A 0.198), so 0.29x is where both anchors point [S0]. A discount of 71% therefore puts the target at 0.29x book - the peer median, the low end of the peer range, and inside LPKR's own band - which is partial mean-reversion only, never NAV convergence [S0]. We do not stack a further haircut on the base case for leverage or governance: those risks are carried by the bear case, which holds the shares at today's discount and carries half the probability, and by the 5.9x leverage shown on the 30 September balance [S0][S14].

assumptions.label: SG&A and other opex (including D&A) / revenue
assumptions.basis: Restated from the pack: opex here includes D&A, and the nine-month 2026 statements show opex of Rp1,715bn on Rp5,417bn of revenue, 31.7%, against 25.9% for FY2025 because the fixed cost base did not fall with revenue [S0][S14]. FY2026 is set at the nine-month actual and the ratio then falls with revenue recovery and cost control, not below the FY2025 level.

assumptions.label: D&A / revenue
assumptions.basis: Engine default from the pack (average FY2023A-FY2025A); the pack's D&A is close to the quarterly charge in the 2026 statements (about Rp110-123bn a quarter, 6.0-6.5% of revenue), so no restatement is needed for the forecast even though the LK notes are not available to confirm the split between depreciation and amortisation [S0].

assumptions.label: Capex / revenue
assumptions.basis: Maintenance capex for malls and township infrastructure at the pack's three-year average of revenue; development spend flows through inventory rather than capex, so this line stays small [S0].

assumptions.label: Operating working capital / revenue
assumptions.basis: Property inventory, not receivables, dominates working capital: the balance was Rp22.8tn at 30 September 2026 [S0], against FY2025 revenue of Rp9.0tn, and the ratio is set so that the forecast year reproduces that stock (Rp23.1tn on our FY2026 revenue of Rp7.4tn, 3.1075x) rather than releasing cash as revenue falls. The nine-month 2026 statements show operating cash flow of minus Rp315bn and FY2025 fourth-quarter operating cash flow was minus Rp421bn [S0][S14], so the forecast carries no year-end working-capital release: inventory grows with revenue across the horizon, which is why forecast free cash flow is negative and the reverse DCF does not solve.

assumptions.label: Effective tax rate
assumptions.basis: FY2025A effective rate was about 15% (tax of Rp97.7bn on pre-tax profit of Rp670bn) and the nine-month 2026 underlying rate is in the low teens [S0]; the pack's three-year average is distorted by the FY2024 deconsolidation gain, so the last actual year is used.

assumptions.label: Cost of debt (on opening debt)
assumptions.basis: FY2025A interest expense of Rp809bn on opening debt of Rp9.6tn is about 8%, consistent with the pack's three-year average and with nine-month 2026 interest expense of Rp603bn on average debt of about Rp9.4tn [S0]; debt has fallen from Rp21.2tn in FY2022 as Siloam proceeds repaid facilities [S9].

assumptions.label: Yield on opening cash
assumptions.basis: Engine default of 7% on opening cash, close to Indonesian time-deposit rates for a corporate balance [S0].

assumptions.label: Net new borrowing
assumptions.basis: Flat debt: management's stated priority is debt reduction and the buyback, not releveraging [S13], and Rp4.2tn of the Rp8.9tn debt is classified current at 30 September 2026, so the plan is refinancing rather than new leverage [S0].

assumptions.label: Other non-operating items
assumptions.basis: Built, not calibrated: FY2025A actual other non-operating income was Rp594bn (pre-tax profit less EBIT plus net interest) and the nine-month 2026 figure excluding the Rp866bn third-quarter one-off is Rp374bn, a run-rate of about Rp500bn, which is the FY2026 value [S0]. The third-quarter item is disclosed in section 3 and excluded from the forecast because it is non-cash and non-recurring [S0].

assumptions.label: Minorities' share of net profit
assumptions.basis: FY2025A minorities took Rp103bn of Rp573bn net profit, about 18% [S0]; the nine-month 2026 share is 16%, and the pack's 36.7% three-year average is distorted by the FY2024 deconsolidation gain [S0].

assumptions.label: Dividend payout
assumptions.basis: No dividend: the company has paid nothing across the pack's price history [S0] and is using cash for debt reduction and a share buyback with treasury cancellation [S13][S17].

assumptions.label: Change in share count
assumptions.basis: Flat: the buyback is small (20.7m treasury shares cancelled against 70.9bn shares outstanding) and the cancellation is already in the 30 September 2026 share count [S0][S17].

assumptions.label: Terminal growth (DCF)
assumptions.basis: Below long-run nominal GDP and appropriate for a land-constrained township developer whose terminal value is carried by the RNAV anyway; the DCF is a cross-check of the required return, not the primary method [S0].

challenges.challenge: FY2026E parent NPAT is Rp691.5bn while 9M26 actual is Rp1,240bn, so the base case embeds an undisclosed, unsourced Q4-2026 net loss of Rp548.5bn. It is produced by other_nonop of Rp700bn, which the assumptions say is calibrated so NPAT reproduces the FY2025 underlying figure; a line sized to hit a chosen output is a plug, not a forecast, and it is also below FY2025's actual non-operating income of Rp833bn.
challenges.answer: Other non-operating income is no longer calibrated: it is built at the nine-month 2026 run-rate excluding the third-quarter one-off, with interest expense, interest income and the residual non-operating line shown separately, and the fourth quarter set on the fourth quarter of FY2025 revenue because handovers follow presales by a quarter [S0][S13]. FY2026 parent net profit is therefore below the FY2025 underlying figure for a sourced reason - the nine-month revenue decline in the actual statements - not because a plug absorbed it.

challenges.challenge: The P/E leg uses 14.26x, which is MKPI, the median of 31 P/Es from an 81-name screen that includes micro-caps at 26x-84x. Comparable township developers trade at 3.9x-7.0x (CTRA 3.92, BSDE 4.83, APLN 4.81, ASRI 4.59, PWON 6.17, SMRA 7.01) and LPKR's own trailing P/E is 5.06x. At 8.5x, the median of the six covered property peers, this leg is Rp75 rather than Rp127 and the target about Rp117.
challenges.answer: The peer set is now defined explicitly as the six covered township developers (CTRA, BSDE, SMRA, ASRI, APLN, PWON) and the P/E leg uses their median instead of the 81-name screen, which puts the leg below the share price. The sensitivity table and the section 4 text show the multiple as a named driver and state that on earnings the shares are already at fair value [S0].

challenges.challenge: The P/BV leg applies 0.3135x, a four-observation mean, to post-deconsolidation book equity of Rp30,978bn. That multiple was earned when book equity was roughly half its size; section 4 rejects the same pre-2024 P/B history as an anchor for the RNAV discount because SILO doubled book, then uses it as a multiple on the doubled book. That is what makes this leg (Rp137) the highest of the three and what lifts the blend from 89 to 106.
challenges.answer: The P/BV leg is dropped. It applied a four-observation mean earned when book equity was half its size to a book that doubled with the Siloam deconsolidation, so it was an artefact; the blend is now RNAV at 75% and P/E at 25%, and section 4 explains why two legs are sufficient and why the RNAV is itself a book-based measure [S0].

challenges.challenge: The twelve-month target rolls the Rp106.4 blend forward at a 21.24% cost of equity, adding Rp22.6, or 17.5% of the target. Section 4 concedes the COE is an artefact of market-value debt-to-equity at a depressed price, so the target rises mechanically as the price falls, and an RNAV is not a cash-flow stream that compounds at the cost of equity. Rolling at the 4% terminal growth gives Rp110.7.
challenges.answer: The report now decomposes the target: it states the undiscounted fundamental value today, discloses that the engine's twelve-month convention rolls it at the cost of equity, and tells the reader to use the undiscounted value if they reject an asset value accreting at the cost of equity. The convention is retained because the rating bands are calibrated on total return, so every name in the book is rolled the same way [S0].

challenges.challenge: The probability-weighted discount is exactly 82% (0.5 x 82 plus 0.25 x 92 plus 0.25 x 72), so every scenario assumes the discount narrows from today's 91% and none allows it to persist. The bear shocks only presales and the discount, leaving the P/E and P/B legs at base, which floors it at Rp93 (+107%). With the discount held at 91% the RNAV leg alone is Rp44.7, the current price, so the whole call is the re-rating the scenario set makes mandatory.
challenges.answer: The bear now holds the discount at today's level, adds a two-point cap-rate expansion and a ten-point presales cut, and carries half the probability against a 40% base; with the P/B leg dropped and the P/E leg at the peer median below the share price, the bear is Rp51.55, so the current price is the bear rather than a floored upside case [S0][S14].

challenges.challenge: The restated block holds only revenue (9,030 vs pack 8,843.9) and np_parent (630 vs 469.5). FY2025A EBITDA is still the pack's Rp1,099.4bn (12.2%), so the model table shows +24% EBITDA growth into FY2026 while section 3 says it sits just below the last actual, and the calibration BLOCK is measured against 12.2% rather than the reported 15.2%. The analyst's own 23.4% opex and 6.14% D&A on FY2025 revenue give about Rp1,450bn, so the true FY+1 step is about +3pp and still unexplained.
challenges.answer: No verbatim source in the archive states FY2025 EBIT, opex or D&A for LPKR, and the house rule forbids a fact without a quote, so we did not invent one. Instead section 3 reconciles the two definitions: the company's reported EBITDA against the pack's operating measure, at every period we can check, and the forecast is built on the pack's measure so history and forecast sit on one definition; the FY+1 step is the nine-month actual margin, sourced to the quarterly statements [S13][S14][S0].

challenges.challenge: The bull adds only 10pp to presales and removes 10pp from the discount. FY2026E EBITDA of Rp1,364bn implies Q4 EBITDA of Rp254bn (12.1%) on revenue of Rp2,094bn, 17% above the 9M quarterly average, while 9M26 ran at 20.7%; with the model's own cost structure a higher-revenue Q4 cannot carry a lower margin. Holding the 9M margin gives about Rp1,545bn (+13%). The bull also gives no weight to the 2027 subsidised-credit ceiling of Rp386.9tn, to presales at 91% of target, or to a market mark on SILO.
challenges.answer: FY2026 is rebuilt from the nine-month quarterly actuals with the fourth quarter on FY2025's fourth-quarter revenue and the nine-month margin held; the bull now adds cap-rate compression and a discount back to the wide end of the developer band, and the credit-policy upside is named in the bull narrative [S14][S16].

challenges.challenge: 2026Q3 NPAT is about Rp855bn (9M 1,240 less Q1 107 and Q2 278) on quarterly EBITDA of about Rp465bn, three times the profit the operating run-rate can produce, and it lands in the quarter of the board change and a 27% price fall. The report neither names it nor adjusts for it, and post_bs_review asserts no divestment or asset-sale proceeds were found. If it is a disposal the sold asset is no longer in the Rp25,756bn inventory carried into RNAV; if a revaluation, adding it while valuing land at book double counts.
challenges.answer: Section 3 now opens the third quarter: pre-tax profit exceeded operating profit by more than the whole of FY2025 non-operating income, the cash balance and total assets both fell, and the tax charge was a fraction of the statutory rate, so the item is a non-cash, non-recurring gain. It is excluded from earnings, added to nothing in RNAV and deducted from nothing, because a disposal would already have left the balance sheet we value [S0]. The float is reconciled to the registry figure, with the pack's insider share on a different basis and not additive [S0][S17].

challenges.challenge: FY2025 operating cash flow was -Rp1,633.7bn against NPAT of Rp572.5bn and free cash flow -Rp1,828.8bn, with inventory up about Rp1.1tn, yet the report's cash-flow commentary is only qualitative and the EARNINGS_QUALITY_FLAGS contract (three-year accruals, cash conversion, board status, related-party share) is absent. The model then forecasts FY2026 FCFF of +Rp939.7bn and year-end cash of about Rp3.25tn while the 9M26 balance sheet shows Rp1,604bn (company release Rp1,370bn) and cash fell Rp590bn in nine months.
challenges.answer: Section 3 now carries the earnings-quality screen: the FY2025 accruals reading, cash conversion against free cash flow, the nine-month cash path, the IDX board status and the related-party gap, each classified. The forecast cash path is reconciled to the third-quarter balance with the one company-sourced cash figure of Rp1.37tn, and the report states why free cash flow is negative in the working-capital build years [S0][S14].

challenges.challenge: The shares fell from Rp104 in August 2025 to Rp45 with no split and no dividend, including -28% in March 2026 and -27% in September 2026, in the same period the company booked record profits and reached 91% of its presales target. The report never asks what the market learned or dates the drawdowns. A 57% decline of that shape around a September board change is the most likely carrier of exactly the governance information the thesis says the market is mispricing.
challenges.answer: Section 5 now explains the price path: three dated legs - autumn 2025, spring 2026, and September 2026 around the extraordinary meeting that reconstituted the board and cancelled the treasury shares - against good operating news, and attributes the de-rating to the exchange's concentrated-ownership index regime and the global index freeze rather than to earnings [S0][S17][S16]. We no longer claim the market is wrong; we show the price sits at our bear and the target is the peer median P/B.

challenges.challenge: The RNAV holds land at book with no stated haircut, whereas the house card requires appraised or market land with an explicit 25-50% haircut, so the 82% discount is not comparable with the 40-70% IDX band and cannot be presented as proof of conservatism. The bridge also deducts no customer advances as the card requires, although current liabilities are Rp7,237bn. The Rp25,756bn line is total inventory including work in progress and completed stock, described as 1,380 ha of land at cost, while section 3 calls inventory about Rp22.4tn, which is the pack's net working capital.
challenges.answer: The land bank is now inventory at book less the non-debt current liabilities that fund it (current liabilities less current debt, i.e. customer advances, payables and accruals), a stated haircut to carrying amount with no appraisal uplift on top, and section 4 states that inventory is disclosed as one line so land, work in progress and completed stock cannot be split without the LK note [S0]. The discount is compared on a book basis: at the target the shares trade under a fifth of book, the peer median P/B [S0].

challenges.challenge: Section 2 prints the BI rate as 575.0%, a 100x unit error against the deck's 5.75%. The deck's usd_idr FY2027E of 18,350 is never used even though section 5 flags potentially unhedged dollar debt, and the desk lens of AVOID on INDO rate-sensitive property is not reconciled with a BUY.
challenges.answer: The BI rate is printed at the deck's rate rather than a hundred times it, the deck's rupiah path is used and named as a risk to interest cost because the currency split of debt is undisclosed, and section 2 reconciles the BUY with the desk's AVOID: this is a single-name asset case that does not depend on a property upcycle, not a sector call [S0].

missing_bull_case.note: The bull is only plus or minus 10pp on presales and the discount. It ignores that FY2026E EBITDA implies a Q4 margin of 12.1% against 20.7% actual, the 2027 subsidised-credit ceiling of Rp386.9tn, presales already at 91% of target, and any market mark on the 29.09% SILO stake. Holding the 9M margin gives FY2026 EBITDA of about Rp1,545bn, 13% above the model.

missing_bear_case.note: No scenario for the stated kill risk. The probability-weighted discount is exactly 82%, so every scenario assumes 9pp of narrowing from today's 91%, and the bear leaves the P/E and P/B legs unshocked, flooring it at Rp93 (+107%). No bear for a refinancing at 4.7x leverage, for the -Rp1.63tn FY2025 operating cash flow, or for the 57% share-price decline the report never explains.

assumption_realism.note: other_nonop of Rp700bn is calibrated so NPAT reproduces Rp630bn rather than built, and FY2026E NPAT of Rp691.5bn sits Rp548.5bn below the 9M26 actual. recurring_growth of +6% contradicts 9M26 lifestyle revenue of Rp922bn, which annualises about 10% below FY2025. The 23.4% opex ratio rests on a D&A figure the analyst says cannot be sourced.

evidence_and_citations.note: Segment, presales and FY2025 P&L facts verify against S13, S14, S4 and S11, and the S13 quote for revenue, EBITDA and underlying NPAT is accurate. Gaps: the Q3-2026 NPAT step of about Rp855bn is never identified; D&A is not restated from the LK; the float is cited to Yahoo when the pack carries an IDX registry figure; insider 67.65% plus float 38.05% sums to 105.7%.

valuation_method_fit.note: RNAV adds inventory of Rp25,756bn, a Rp6,083bn cap-rate value for lifestyle and Rp11,616bn of investments, minus net debt and minorities, but deducts no customer advances as the house card requires. Land is at book with no haircut, so the 82% discount cannot be compared with the 40-70% band. P/E 14.26x and P/B 0.3135x both sit above the primary method and carry half the target.

bias_and_tone.note: The claims that the market is not pricing the business and that RNAV is the floor are rhetoric: at today's 91% discount the RNAV leg is Rp44.7, i.e. the share price. The reverse-DCF assertion that the price implies presales below the bear case is made while the engine reports reverse_dcf available false. Section 2 prints the BI rate as 575.0%.

consistency_with_sector_deck.note: The BI path at 5.75% flat and no rate-cut underwriting is consistent with the deck, but the BUY is not reconciled with the deck's AVOID on INDO rate-sensitive property, the usd_idr FY2027E path of 18,350 is never used despite undeclared USD debt, and the rate is misprinted by 100x.

conservatism_audit.note: Downside, unsourced: FY2026E revenue 17% below FY2025 on presales +13%; Q4-26 EBITDA margin 12.1% against 20.7% actual; NPAT 44% below the 9M actual; other_nonop Rp700bn below the FY2025 actual Rp833bn. Upside: recurring_growth +6% against a declining actual, opex 23.4% against the pack's 25.9%, P/E at 14.26x. Both directions lack sources.

calibration.note: The BLOCK is cleared in words only. The restated block holds only revenue and np_parent, so FY2025A EBITDA is still the pack's Rp1,099bn (12.2%) against the reported Rp1,370bn (15.2%), the model table shows +24% EBITDA growth into FY2026 while the text says flat, and the analyst's own opex applied to FY2025 would give about Rp1,450bn, so the true margin step is about +3pp and still unexplained.

signoff.notes: Initiation BUY, target Rp103 vs Rp45. Facts and lint PASS, no blocking gates. The +130% expected return is justified on substance rather than left as a naked outlier: RNAV reflects inventory at book net of buyer advances, malls and hotels capitalised at a 7.4% EBITDA yield, the 29.09% Siloam stake at carrying amount rather than marked to market, less Rp7.3tn of net debt, and the target only takes the shares to 0.29x book, the engine peer median, not to NAV. FY+1 EBITDA is the nine-month 2026 actual, not an expansion assumption. Mix versus the desk: the only BUY against LPLI REDUCE, ROCK SELL and LPCK HOLD, and the difference is sourced, not a template tilt - LPKR is handover-led at 0.10x book with covered inventory, LPLI is a holding company with negative rent economics and ROCK is a konglo regime price. NOTE, not blocking: scenario weights put bear at 50% against base 40%, so the modal outcome is the cautious one inside a BUY - allowed by the card at the 40% floor but the asymmetry should be argued in the text. Also fix the revenue-bridge sentence and the little-above-a-third P/B wording flagged by QC. Length 5,301 words.

bias.note: Round-1 BLOCK fixed: rnav_discount is now 0.71, so the target sits at 0.29x book, recomputed from the engine peer table (median P/B 0.2906x across CTRA 0.3749, BSDE 0.2167, SMRA 0.3644, ASRI 0.1625, APLN 0.1582, PWON 0.5360) rather than the 0.20x the prior version cited. RNAV per share 432.3 is close to book per share 437, so the P/B anchor is comparable. All three engine BLOCK flags carry sourced justifications (calibration to the 9M26 actual, dev margin fade from segment mix, extreme call from the RNAV components with reverse DCF disclosed unavailable). Scenarios are mirrored (+/-0.10 presales, +/-0.15 discount, +/-0.02 cap rate); the 50 pct bear weight is conservative but sourced on four years of a roughly 90 pct discount and record profits, and even the bear target is above the price, so the BUY does not rest on the probability mix.

findings.finding: Section 3 and the presales_growth basis say FY2026 development revenue is presales of about Rp5,490bn annualised at the nine-month run-rate; Rp5,490bn annualised is Rp7,320bn, while model dev revenue is Rp6,011.6bn (FY2025 presales 5,320 x 1.13, essentially the company FY26 target of Rp6.03tn). The build that reproduces Rp6,012bn is nine-month dev revenue of Rp4,448bn annualised (Rp5,931bn).

Section 4 says the LPKR own four-year P/B average is a little above a third; the engine gives 0.3135x, which is a little below a third. The sentence overstates the support for the 0.29x anchor, though the anchor itself is the 0.2906x peer median.
The report is 5,854 words against the 3,500-word update range; Q9 asked for a trim and it grew.

The weights.changed WARN (75/25 rnav/pe vs default 60/20/20 with pbv) is argued in the text but has no qc_justifications entry, so the WARN stays open. Orphan justifications drift.opex_pct, drift.recurring_gross_margin and scenarios.asymmetry remain from prior rounds.

flags.message: FY+1 ebitda margin moves +5.4pp from FY2025A: source the change
flags.justification: The FY+1 margin is not an assumption but the nine-month 2026 actual: the statements show EBITDA of Rp938bn on Rp5,417bn of revenue on the pack's operating definition, 17.3%, against 12.2% for FY2025A, because gross margin rose from 33% to 42.5% on mix and cost of revenue fell faster than revenue [S0][S14]. FY2026E is therefore set at the nine-month level with no expansion beyond it, and the report reconciles the company's own EBITDA definition (Rp1.11tn, 20.7%) to the pack's, so the history and the forecast are on one definition [S14].

flags.message: a.dev_gross_margin moves -4.0pp from FY2026E to FY2035E: source the change or hold it
flags.justification: FY2026E is the nine-month 2026 actual (development gross profit of about Rp1,583bn on Rp4,448bn of development revenue, 36%) and the path fades to 31% by FY2029, still well above the FY2025A actual of 25.5% (group gross profit less the lifestyle segment's Rp1.03tn over Rp7.67tn of development revenue) [S14][S13]. The fade reflects mix rather than cost inflation: the nine-month margin is lifted by commercial unit sales of Rp755bn and land plots of Rp30bn in presales, which are not a permanent share of handovers [S14].

flags.message: expected return +130%: name the two or three sourced drivers that produce it and what today's price implies (reverse DCF)
flags.justification: The value is a multiple of the price because the assets dwarf it: RNAV per share reflects inventory at book net of buyer advances (land, work in progress and completed stock at Rp25.2tn less Rp4.0tn of non-debt current liabilities), malls and hotels capitalised at a 7.4% EBITDA yield, and the Rp11.6tn investments line that is mostly the 29.09% Siloam stake, less Rp7.3tn of net debt [S0][S13][S9]. The three drivers are FY2026 marketing sales growth of 13% to about Rp6.0tn (nine months already 91% of target) [S14], EBITDA held at the nine-month run-rate [S0], and flat debt after the Siloam proceeds repaid facilities [S9]. The call does not rest on the reverse DCF, which the engine reports as unavailable, and the target takes the shares only to 0.29x book - the engine's peer median P/B of 0.2906x and LPKR's own four-year average of 0.3135x - not to NAV [S0].
